data.narrative:
Radical AI is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $55M to date. The target operates within a competitive sector landscape comprising 1 public comparable and 8 private peers, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI. The founding team combines deep domain expertise: CEO Joseph F. Krause brings neuromorphic semiconductor research from Army Research Lab and prior deep-tech venture experience; Chief Scientist Prof. Gerbrand Ceder holds 25 years of materials science credentials from MIT and UC Berkeley.

Given the early-stage profile and limited peer visibility at identical stage and valuation tier, peer-median benchmarking was not feasible—the comparable universe contained insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints to support a robust cross-check. Consequently, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier (typical for Seed to next-stage advancement) to the $55M capital raised proxy yields an implied valuation of $138M.

This analysis supports a range of $117M to $158M, centered on $138M. The valuation reflects capital deployed and typical early-stage progression dynamics, but carries material uncertainty around market traction and product-market fit validation, which remain unspecified in available data. Investors should prioritize primary diligence on near-term technical milestones and customer commitments to calibrate stage-appropriate risk.
